content.text: Workers in Mugsborough produce society’s goods but receive wages too small to buy them back, while capitalists accumulate wealth, cause overproduction, and dismiss laborers. Owen explains this “Money Trick” and argues for Socialism, though fellow workers mock him. Unemployment brings hunger, charity, workhouses, exploitation, and family breakdown. Ruth is assaulted by Slyme after Easton abandons her at the Cricketers pub. Owen’s family and the Lindens endure severe poverty; Mary Linden enters a rented room while Jack and his wife enter the workhouse. Owen, ill and coughing blood, contemplates killing himself and his family to spare them future misery. Employers and civic leaders meanwhile manipulate newspapers, charities, councils, and electric-light schemes for profit. At Sweater’s office they plan to sell failing works to the town, while at “The Cave” local businessmen gather to coordinate corruption and display their ignorance.
